title: Drift-Constrained Optimization: Only Direction Matters in Fine-Tuning Instruct Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.13680v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Fine-tuning instruct models often improves target performance while inducing behavioral drift from the reference model, which can degrade existing capabilities. Rather than treating this drift as an uncontrolled consequence of optimization, we specify a behavioral drift budget before optimization and ask how to boost the target-task performance within it. Locally, behavioral drift induces a shared geometry anchored at the reference model, with the drift budget defining a boundary within this space. In this space, drift determines distance from the reference, leaving update direction as the remaining degree of freedom. Fine-tuning updates can therefore be compared through their directional efficiency, naturally reformulating fine-tuning as a direction-selection problem. This reformulation makes a concrete prediction: changing the accessible directions can qualitatively alter the outcome of fine-tuning. We test this prediction in a stringe

translated_title: 漂移约束优化：指令模型微调中唯有方向至关重要
translated_abstract: 微调指令模型通常能提升目标任务性能，但同时会引发相对于参考模型的行为漂移，这可能会损害模型已有的能力。我们不再将这种漂移视为优化的不受控结果，而是在优化之前设定一个行为漂移预算，并探讨如何在该预算范围内提升目标任务性能。在局部上，行为漂移诱导出一种以参考模型为锚点的共享几何结构，漂移预算则定义了该空间中的一个边界。在这个空间中，漂移决定了与参考模型的距离，因而更新方向成为剩下的唯一自由度。因此，微调更新可以通过其方向效率进行比较，从而自然地将微调重新表述为一个方向选择问题。这一重新表述给出了一个具体的预测：改变可访问的方向可以从根本上改变微调的结果。我们在严格的（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文将指令模型微调中的行为漂移转化为预先设定的预算约束，在漂移空间中把微调重新表述为方向选择问题，并证明改变可访问的更新方向能够定性地改变微调结果。
en_tdlr: The paper reformulates fine-tuning of instruct models as a direction-selection problem within a pre-specified behavioral drift budget, showing that changing accessible update directions can qualitatively alter fine-tuning outcomes.
